newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks defence cooperation with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks defence cooperation with Iran.

text.p: NATO member Turkey has discussed defence industry cooperation with neighbouring Iran, a Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Various cooperation opportunities between Turkey and Iran were dealt with during Mr Boroujerdi's visit to our ministry. Defence industry cooperation...was only one of them," spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Tuesday met Iran's deputy foreign minister, Alaeddin Boroujerdi, who came to Ankara ahead of a visit by Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani later this month.
Boroujerdi told reporters after the meeting that the two countries' defence ministers had held talks in Tehran in August during a visit to Iran by Erbakan.

Spokesman Atacanli said defence cooperation might be discussed during Rafsanjani's visit but he gave no more details. Defence Ministry officials declined to comment on any defence cooperation with Iran.

Ankara sealed a military training deal with Israel in February which drew sharp criticism from Arab countries and Iran. Turkey also has a defence industry agreement with the Jewish state under which Israel is to modernise Turkish air force F-4 jets.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has promised to improve relations with the country's Moslem neighbours.
Turkey and Iran signed a $23 billion gas deal that angered Ankara's close ally the United States when Erbakan visited Tehran.
